subject: Sequenced reserve playbook & sprint plan for GPU capacity
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Miller <ava.miller@crestwave.ai>, Logan Price <logan.price@crestwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sequenced reserve playbook & sprint plan for GPU capacity

Hi Ava / Logan —

Following our demo, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan that sequences evaluation milestones into a reserve commitment runway. The goals:

- Ensure CrestWave has predictable latency for peak inference (P99 targets) during pilot and GA.
- Minimize your upfront spend by phasing GPU tranche commits tied to evaluation gates.
- Deliver a reproducible onboarding sprint so your infra and security teams can validate Private deployment in parallel.

Highlights in the attached: MAP tab (milestones + owner), Lead times tab (Dedicated vs Private procurement/VM images), and GPU pool sizing appendix (sprint-by-sprint throughput estimates).

Key asks for this week:
1) Confirm targeted GA window (we used Aug 16 in the doc as a placeholder).
2) Approve the initial evaluation tranche: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for 4 weeks (staging + load tests).
3) Share your procurement SLA constraints — e.g., PO timing, legal review lead time.

If agreeable, we can convert tranche 1 into a 30-day reserved commit that guarantees the capacity window and gives you preferred pricing.

I looped in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (capacity planning) to align on sizing and lead times.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk the MAP live.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: CrestWave_MAP_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: Ava Miller <ava.miller@crestwave.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Price <logan.price@crestwave.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 12:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sequenced reserve playbook & sprint plan for GPU capacity

Hi Camila —

Thanks for this. A few quick clarifying questions after a skim:

- The MAP shows "Private lead time: 6–8 weeks" and "Dedicated lead time: 2–3 weeks". Can you confirm what triggers the longer Private path (is it network/VPC setup or E2E security reviews)?
- For tranche sizing: the 8 A100-equivalent for tranche 1 looks reasonable, but are those raw GPUs or accounting for quantized model variants? We need to understand token throughput for our 1M daily user target.
- On procurement: our legal wants to see a draft SOW and SAAS addendum before committing; how fast can you get that?

Happy to do a call Monday.

Best,
Ava
Head of Product, CrestWave
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sequenced reserve playbook & sprint plan for GPU capacity (internal)

Quick internal notes to align on Ava's Qs before the call: 

1) Private vs Dedicated lead time:
   - Private (VPC/on-prem) longer mainly due to customer-side networking (VPC peering, subnets, CIDR planning) and KMS/HSM onboarding; also we include a security readiness review that usually takes 3–4 weeks on top of networking. We should list the security artifacts CrestWave must provide (SOC2 evidence, IP allowlist ranges, sample logs).

2) GPU sizing nuance:
   - The 8 A100-equivalent in tranche 1 is a conservative baseline assuming FP16 runtime. If they select 4-bit quantized variants we can bump effective throughput ~1.6–1.8x — we should present both raw and quantized ops in the appendix.
   - For 1M DAUs and expected prompt mix, our ops model estimates ~120 tokens/sec per A100 for their median prompt; show 95th percentile numbers for concurrency planning.

3) SOW & docs: I can produce a one-page SOW template (scope + success criteria + tranche commitments) and a security checklist today; Marissa can confirm lead-time language.

Action items for the call: finalize GA date, lock tranche 1 start window (we propose July 12–Aug 8), and agree on procurement milestones (PO, legal, invoice cadence).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Miller <ava.miller@crestwave.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sequenced reserve playbook & sprint plan for GPU capacity

Hi Ava —

Following Ben's outline, a concrete lead-time playbook: 

- Dedicated (hosted) path: 10 business days to provision once PO + signed SOW received. This includes reserved pool + routing policy configuration and a kickoff for traffic shaping tests.

- Private (VPC) path: 6 weeks baseline (networking + security validation + KMS integration). If CrestWave can commit to a network runbook and provide their KMS onboarding window in week 1, we can target 4 weeks.

GPU pool phasing recommendation (sprint model):
- Sprint A (Eval): 8 A100-eq | 4 weeks | purpose: capability + load tests
- Sprint B (Pilot): add 16 A100-eq | 6 weeks | purpose: scaled performance and early GA traffic shadowing
- Sprint C (GA reserve): additional 32 A100-eq (staggered) | long-term reserve

Pricing note: converting Sprint A to a 30-day reserved commit secures 15% unit discount and guarantees the capacity window.

I've attached a condensed GPU pool breakdown PDF for their procurement team.

If CrestWave can sign a narrow SOW that binds Sprint A schedule and payment terms, we can lock tranche 1 on July 12 start. Please confirm PO cadence and preferred invoice terms (net30/net45).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: GPU_pool_breakdown_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Logan Price <logan.price@crestwave.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sequenced reserve playbook & sprint plan for GPU capacity

Camila / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. We're aligned on the phased approach and the trigger-based tranche commits. A few quick confirmations from our side:

- CrestWave intends to approve Sprint A (8 GPUs) as a 30-day reserved commit conditional on receiving the one-page SOW and a security checklist by EOD Tuesday.
- Logistics: legal will aim for a redline turn of 7 business days once they receive the SOW. Procurement is fine with net30 invoice terms.
- Network readiness: we can commit to providing CIDR ranges and a point person for KMS onboarding within 3 business days after the SOW is sent.

I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Tuesday 11am ET to walk through the MAP and sign off on milestones; please confirm availability.

Appreciate the speed — this gives us a clean runway to a mid-August GA if sprints go as planned.

—Logan
Logan Price
VP of Engineering, CrestWave
